text:
In 1975, 30 dominant males were observed on two dancing grounds upon Tract II; based on these observations, the total estimated spring population was 120 birds, or approximately five birds per square mile. Tract II has not been studied as intensively as Tract III, and it is possible that other dancing grounds may be present.
Sage grouse have not been observed on either Tract II or Tract III. This area is probably not good sage grouse habitat as they require extensive sagebrush plains. Martin (1975) located three sage grouse leks in Sarpy Basin north of the leases. He stated that the 11.7 males per lek was an indication of poor sage grouse habitat as the average for south eastern Montana is 43.2 sage grouse males per lek.
Ring-necked pheasants are common, particularly in the valleys of Sarpy and East Sarpy Creeks. Creek bottom thickets in combination with agricultural land provide good habitat for pheasants. Observations and crowing count data indicate that few pheasants are present on Tract II, probably as a result of poor habitat conditions. On Tract III, pheasants have been observed primarily on the eastern portion of the lease and along major drainageways.
Gray or Hungarian partridges have been observed in the area in small numbers. Sufficient data are not available to describe habitat use, but agricultural areas in the valleys of Sarpy and East Sarpy creeks and the eastern portion of Tract III offer the most attractive habitat for this species.
Four species of ducks, the mallard, green-winged teal, blue-winged teal and shoveler have been observed in the Project Area. Lack of suitable aquatic habitat undoubtedly limits use of the area by waterfowl, although limited nesting occurs where wetland habitat is available.
